score.note: Fourth pass: re-verified the third pass's trampoline-call fix with --align and confirmed it resolved open question (a) below (the 5th-argument-in-r4 / w,h-on-stack calling convention at every Func_080072f4 site now matches byte-for-byte; every remaining diff around those call sites is downstream of the register-allocation issue in (b), not the calling convention itself). Found one genuine, verified improvement on the (b) register-allocation question: the 512-slot `-1` sentinel-init loop had its own block-scoped `s32 n;` counter, distinct from the outer-scope `i` already reused by both the ring-seed loop and the final 512-particle scan loop. The reference physically coalesces all of these short, disjoint-lifetime loop counters into a single register (`sl`); giving the sentinel-init loop its own separate `n` identity instead of reusing `i` was preventing that coalescing on the candidate side. Removing `n` and reusing `i` for that loop too (matching the other two) dropped differing_halfwords 298->296 and wrong_instructions 316->308 with no size change (828 bytes). Tried extending the same idea to `member` (the 8-member loop counter, also coalesced into `sl` by the reference) by reusing `i` for it as well: this regressed sharply (296->334, size 828->836) and was reverted -- `member`'s live range interacts with `fp`/the burst/target_slot nested blocks differently enough that forcing it through the same pseudo as `i` confuses the allocator rather than helping it. Also retried, now that the trampoline fix has changed the function's overall RTL shape, several of the specific tie-break experiments already recorded as failed against the pre-trampoline-fix code in notes (b) and rejected_experiments below (member/fp declaration order, block-scoping member into the 8-member loop's own block, splitting the `fp >= member*4+8` compound condition, reordering the fp=0/accumulator=0x8000 initializer statements, and hoisting `ring = work+0x7080` above the preceding Func_080041d8 call to match an instruction-scheduling difference seen at the very start of the ring-seed setup): every one of these still has zero effect except the last two, which measurably regressed (296->297 and 296->299 respectively) and were reverted. This confirms (b) remains a genuinely open, not-yet-cracked cross-family compiler register-allocation-priority question even after the trampoline fix -- it is not merely a downstream artifact of the old Func_080072f4 mismodeling.

family.actual_sibling_evidence: Confirmed member of the 0x03001eec 'battle work' subsystem family documented in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080e7404.json, 080d59b0.json, 080d82b0.json and 080dc1ec.json: identical Func_080cd594(mode)/Func_080e0524(id,target,f,f)/Func_080041d8(0x080CD261,0x480)/Func_08004278(0x080CD261)/Func_08002dd8(id)/Func_080cdbc0() shape, the same *(void**)0x03001EEC/0x03001EF0/0x03001EF4 work/draw_destination/extra_target globals as 080d82b0, and the same Func_080cef64(flag, out_pair) call as 080dc1ec. Per the already-adopted games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/runtime/runtime_owner_21.c, this is not dynamic callback resolution: Func_080cef64 unconditionally copies Data_03001e50[46] then Data_03001e50[47] (the kind-46/47 allocator-cache slot values, already populated by earlier Func_080ed408 calls) into out_pair[0]/out_pair[1]; flag only selects which Func_080ed408 load parameters populated those slots beforehand. This owner's callbacks[2] array is correctly sized (2 words) and both entries are genuinely read back downstream as draw callbacks -- unlike 080dc1ec's single-word `callback` local, which undersized the same two-word write by one word until corrected. This confirms the shared family header should model Func_080cef64 as a two-word allocator-cache-slot copy, not a callback-table resolver.

rejected_experiments: A leftover dead-code assignment (`member_id_offset = 36 + member * 2` inside the wrong loop, a copy-paste artifact from re-deriving the member_id_offset stepping used by the second, count-driven loop) was caught and removed before the first scoring pass since it did not correspond to any instruction in the reference and only accidentally left the score unchanged when present.

Tried modeling the second Func_080072f4 site (member-ring draw) with `callbacks[1]`, matching the final 512-particle-scan site: this looked plausible (two distinct blit routines, one per draw 'kind') but the reference's own instruction stream contradicts it -- both the orbiting-marker draw and the member-ring draw load their 5th argument from the SAME stack slot (`sp+32` in the reference's 40-byte frame) that holds `callbacks[0]`; only the 512-particle scan differs, and it reaches `callbacks[1]` through a saved pointer (`ldr r0,[sp,#20]; ldr r4,[r0,#4]`) rather than a second direct array read. Reproducing that split -- `callbacks[0]` at both early sites, `callback_ptr[1]` (a retained `DrawRectangleFn *callback_ptr = callbacks;` passed to Func_080cef64 and re-dereferenced later) at the last one -- is what makes all three Func_080072f4 5th-argument loads match in shape.

Tried leaving `work`/`draw_destination`/`extra_target` as three independent `*(void**)literal` reads (the original shape): the reference's actual prologue is a `heap_cache = (void**)0x03001EEC; cursor = heap_cache; work = *cursor++; draw_destination = *cursor;` pair (byte-identical `ldmia r3!,{r1}` sequence) with `extra_target` read separately off the retained `heap_cache` base (`heap_cache[2]`, `ldr r2,[r2,#8]`) rather than its own literal pool entry. The three-independent-loads shape cannot produce the reference's `ldmia`/register-offset instructions no matter what register `work` lands in.

Tried a plain `for (i = 0; i != 32; i++)` reusing the outer-scope `i` for the innermost particle-burst loop (nested inside the 8-member ring loop): this makes the compiler treat `i`'s pseudo as spanning from the top-level ring-seed loop all the way to the bottom-level 512-particle scan, which collides with `member`'s live range across the burst and forces extra spills. Giving the burst loop its own block-scoped `burst` counter (never reused elsewhere) removed that collision and measurably improved the score (differing_halfwords 341->319, candidate size 840->836); the reference's own burst-loop counter is a low register (r4) entirely separate from the sl-based counter it reuses for the ring-seed/member/final-scan loops, which is consistent with treating it as its own variable rather than a shared `i`.

Tried moving `target_slot`/`member_id_offset` from function scope into the target_slot-loop's own block (matching the pattern that helped `burst`): this had zero effect on the score, confirming that block *scoping* alone does not change this compiler's register allocation -- what mattered for `burst` was giving it a genuinely distinct variable identity, not narrower lexical scope.

Fourth pass, post-trampoline-fix retries of the open (b) tie-break, all confirmed zero-effect or regressions: reusing the outer-scope `i` for `member` too (296->334, size grew 828->836, reverted -- unlike the successful `n`->`i` merge for the sentinel-init loop, `member`'s live range genuinely conflicts with the nested burst/target_slot blocks); declaring `fp` before `member` at function scope (zero effect, reconfirming the pre-trampoline-fix finding still holds); block-scoping `member` into its own nested block inside the 8-member do-while (zero effect, generalizing the target_slot scoping-alone finding above to this variable too); renaming the `fp` C variable to `pass_idx` (zero effect, as expected -- confirms the compiler's choice is not driven by the identifier colliding with the ARM register mnemonic); rewriting `fp >= member*4+8` as `member*4+8 <= fp` (zero effect); swapping the `fp = 0;`/`accumulator = 0x8000;` initializer order (296->297, reverted); hoisting `ring = (u8*)work+0x7080;` to before the preceding `Func_080041d8(...)` call, matching an instruction-scheduling difference seen in the reference at that point (`bl Func_080041d8` is scheduled after two independent `ring`-base-computing instructions in the reference, but after the call in the candidate) (296->299, reverted). None of these source-level knobs move `member` off `fp` or the outer pass counter off the stack; the register-allocation-priority question in note (b) below remains genuinely open.

Semantic summary: the most elaborate of the four sub-effects. Sets hardware alpha-blend register 0x04000052, resolves a pair of draw callbacks via Func_080cef64, opens three effect registrations via Func_080e0524 (against extra_target, work, and work+0x320), seeds a 32-slot ring at work+0x7080 with randomized radii/heights and a 512-slot shared particle pool's lifetime sentinel, then runs 96 animation passes. Each pass draws one orbiting marker at a fp-derived sine/cosine angle, then walks up to 8 fixed member slots, drawing and advancing each ring entry once its per-slot activation threshold (`fp >= member*4+8`) is crossed. IMPORTANT CORRECTION from the first draft: once a given ring entry's height crosses 95 and a burst of 32 fresh particles is spawned into that member's private sub-range, the SAME pass -- gated behind that burst, not once per outer frame -- also stamps `work[0x77A8]=4` and, if the target has any real party members, cues Func_080d6888/Func_080b5088 for every one of them from the target's own count field (confirmed from the reference's own labels: the `.L5` convergence point that all three inner guards funnel to sits AFTER this block, and the block itself is only reachable by falling out of the burst loop). Finally the pass scans all 512 shared particle slots, drawing and aging every slot whose lifetime sentinel is not -1.

The member-activation gate (`fp >= member * 4 + 8`) and the hard 8-member cap on the ring/particle-burst loop (independent of the target's real member count, which only gates the separate Func_080d6888/Func_080b5088 loop) are both taken directly from the reference's literal comparisons rather than simplified, since the point is reproducing the compiled shape.

Three of the four open questions carried over from the other owners in this family are now resolved for this owner specifically and worth propagating: (1) the Func_080e0524 id argument is `(s32)&Value_XXXXXXXX`, not a plain int literal, at every call site in this owner (matches the already-adopted Value_000000b4 idiom in puff_arc/run.c) -- 080d59b0/080d82b0/080dc1ec's still-open Func_080e0524 calls should be checked against the same idiom; (2) the work/draw_destination/extra_target prologue is a heap_cache+cursor pair, not three independent absolute reads, whenever all three globals are read together -- 080d82b0's identical three-global prologue is the most likely other beneficiary; (3) `DrawRectangleFn callbacks[2]`-style locals are read through a retained pointer variable (`callback_ptr[1]`), not a second direct array index, for whichever call site is compiled latest/deepest in the function -- seen here and structurally likely in 080dc1ec's `callback_pair[2]`.

Open question (a) from the second/third pass -- the 5th-argument-in-r4 calling convention at every Func_080072f4/trampoline site -- is now RESOLVED as a side effect of the third pass's trampoline-call fix, and reconfirmed with --align in the fourth pass: every Func_080072f4 call site's argument-loading sequence (dest/src/x/y in r0-r3, callback pointer loaded into r4 from its stack slot immediately before the `bl`, w/h pre-stored to sp+0/sp+4) now matches the reference byte-for-byte. It was never really a distinct ABI question -- it was a downstream symptom of modeling the calls as a fictional direct 7-argument function instead of real indirect calls through `callbacks[0]`/`callback_ptr[1]`. One open question remains genuinely stuck after real attempts across two passes, not low-confidence guessing: (b) A persistent 4-byte stack-frame overshoot (`sub sp,#44` vs the reference's `#40`): the reference keeps its outer 96-pass loop counter in the real `fp`/r11 register for the whole function and reuses `sl` for every disjoint-lifetime short loop counter in the function (the 32-iteration ring-seed loop, the 512-iteration sentinel-init loop, the 8-iteration member loop, and the final 512-iteration particle-scan loop); this candidate's compiler instead puts the 8-member loop's `member` counter in `fp` and spills the outer pass counter to a stack slot. The fourth pass found that merging the sentinel-init loop's separately-declared `n` counter into the already-shared `i` identity (which the ring-seed and final-scan loops already used) helped the allocator coalesce that one loop into the same register family the reference uses, improving the score measurably -- but the analogous merge for `member` regressed sharply instead of helping, and every other tie-break lever tried across both passes (member/fp declaration order, block scoping at multiple granularities, renaming `fp` away from the ARM register mnemonic, restating the compound guard condition, reordering initializer statements, hoisting an independent computation above a call site to chase an observed scheduling difference) had zero effect or regressed. This is best treated now as a genuinely open, evidence-exhausted-at-the-source-level compiler register-allocation-priority question, consistent with its framing as a cross-family issue also affecting 080dc1ec, 080d82b0, and 080d59b0 -- it likely needs either compiler-internals-level investigation (out of scope for a source-only reconstruction pass) or a source restructuring idea neither pass has tried yet. How the second Func_080072f4 argument (src) should be typed once a shared work-block header exists remains open too -- here it alternates between a plain work-relative offset (`work`, `work+800`) and an extra_target-relative table lookup (`extra_target + Data_080ede48[idx-1]`), exactly mirroring the split already seen in 080d59b0/080d82b0/080dc1ec.
